title: Your first MCP server
intro: Wrap the chatbot's tools into a server any MCP app can use — with FastMCP doing the protocol work.

steps.title: Two requests, two ways to build
steps.body:
A tools server answers two request types: **ListToolsRequest** ("what do you have?") and **CallToolRequest** ("run this one").

- **Low-level**: handle those request types directly — full control over every aspect.
- **FastMCP**: a high-level interface — *you just write functions*; FastMCP handles the protocol.

steps.title: Functions become tools
steps.body:
```python
mcp = FastMCP("research")

@mcp.tool()
def search_papers(topic: str, max_results: int = 5) -> List[str]:
    """Search arXiv for papers on a topic and store their info."""
    ...
```

> [!key] The **type hints and docstring become the tool schema** the client sees. One source of truth — no handwritten JSON.

steps.title: A real project, run with uv
steps.body: The research server gets its own project: `uv init`, a virtual environment, `uv add mcp arxiv`, code in `research_server.py`, and `mcp.run(transport="stdio")` at the bottom — local servers speak stdio and get launched by their client as a subprocess.

viz.title: From chatbot function to shared tool

points.label: Write fn
points.note: The same search_papers / extract_info the Lesson-3 chatbot called directly.

points.label: Run stdio
points.note: mcp.run(transport='stdio') — the client will spawn this file.

points.label: Inspect
points.note: npx @modelcontextprotocol/inspector — list and call the tools by hand.

steps.title: Inspector before client
steps.body:
The **MCP inspector** is a browser UI that connects to your server, lists its capabilities, and invokes tools interactively — the fastest feedback loop in MCP development.

> [!tip] After the refactor, the chatbot keeps only query processing and the chat loop. The tools now live where they belong: on a server **any** MCP-compatible app can use.

recap:
**FastMCP: write functions, get a protocol-compliant server.**

- Two canonical requests: list tools, call tool.
- Signatures + docstrings ARE the schema.
- Local servers run stdio and are launched by their clients.
- Always smoke-test with the inspector before building a client.
